back: A cost that does not change with output in the short run (rent, insurance, salaries, loan repayments).
A cost that changes directly with output (materials, packaging, wages paid per item).
A direct cost can be traced to a product or job; an indirect cost (overhead) is shared by many products.
A cost with a fixed part and a variable part, such as electricity with a standing charge plus a charge per unit.
Total cost = fixed cost + variable cost.
Marginal cost = change in total cost ÷ change in output; the extra cost of one more unit.
Fixed cost is spread over more units, so fixed cost per unit falls as output rises.
Pricing, special orders, cost control, performance measurement and deciding whether to continue a product.
